review.plain: Defines premises, building, dwelling, night, and entering or remaining unlawfully for the burglary and trespass article.
Trespass is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in or upon premises; it is a violation.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in or upon premises

penalties.penalty: Violation (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in or upon premises

review.plain: Criminal trespass in the third degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in fenced property, schools, camps, public housing or posted railroad zones under listed circumstances; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property

penalties.penalty: Class B misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property
conditions: The building or real property is fenced or otherwise enclosed in a manner designed to exclude intruders

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property
conditions: The building is utilized as an elementary or secondary school or a children's overnight camp or a summer day camp as defined in section one thousand three hundred ninety-two of the public health law
The entry is in violation of conspicuously posted rules or regulations governing entry and use thereof

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property
conditions: The building or real property is located within a city with a population in excess of one million and is utilized as an elementary or secondary school
The entry is in violation of a personally communicated request to leave the premises from a principal, custodian or other person in charge thereof

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property
conditions: The building or real property is located outside of a city with a population in excess of one million and is utilized as an elementary or secondary school
The entry is in violation of a personally communicated request to leave the premises from a principal, custodian, school board member or trustee, or other person in charge thereof

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property

The entry is in violation of conspicuously posted rules or regulations governing entry and use thereof

The entry is in violation of a personally communicated request to leave the premises from a housing police officer or other person in charge thereof

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property
conditions: The property consists of a right-of-way or yard of a railroad or rapid transit railroad which has been designated and conspicuously posted as a no-trespass railroad zone

review.plain: Criminal trespass in the second degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a dwelling, or a level two or three registered sex offender entering the school their victim attends or attended; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: nters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
enters or remains in a public or private elementary, parochial, intermediate, junior high, vocational or high school

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
Enters or remains in a public or private elementary, parochial, intermediate, junior high, vocational or high school
exceptions: The person is a lawfully registered student at such school
The person is a lawful student participant in a school sponsored event
The person is a parent or a legal guardian of a lawfully registered student at such school and enters the school for the purpose of attending their child's or dependent's event or activity
Such school is the person's designated polling place and he or she enters such school building for the limited purpose of voting
The person enters such school building for the limited purposes authorized by the superintendent or chief administrator of such school
crimes.who: A person required to maintain registration under article six-C of the correction law and designated a level two or level three offender pursuant to subdivision six of section one hundred sixty-eight-l of the correction law
knowledge: Knowing that the victim of the offense for which such registration is required attends or formerly attended such school

review.plain: Criminal trespass in the first degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a building while possessing, or knowing a participant possesses, an explosive, deadly weapon, or loaded-capable firearm; it is a class D felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building
Possesses, or knows that another participant in the crime possesses, an explosive or a deadly weapon

Possesses a firearm, rifle or shotgun, as those terms are defined in section 265.00, and also possesses or has readily accessible a quantity of ammunition which is capable of being discharged from such firearm, rifle or shotgun

penalties.penalty: Class D felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: In the course of committing such crime, the person possesses, or knows that another participant in the crime possesses, an explosive or a deadly weapon

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: In the course of committing such crime, the person possesses a firearm, rifle or shotgun, as those terms are defined in section 265.00, and also possesses or has readily accessible a quantity of ammunition which is capable of being discharged from such firearm, rifle or shotgun

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: In the course of committing such crime, the person knows that another participant in the crime possesses a firearm, rifle or shotgun under circumstances described in subdivision two

review.plain: Burglary in the third degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a building with intent to commit a crime there; it is a class D felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building

intent: With intent to commit a crime therein

penalties.penalty: Class D felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building

acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building

intent: With intent to commit a crime therein

penalties.penalty: Class C felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the building or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime is armed with explosives or a deadly weapon

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the building or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime causes physical injury to any person who is not a participant in the crime

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the building or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime uses or threatens the immediate use of a dangerous instrument

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a building
conditions: The building is a dwelling

review.plain: Burglary in the first degree is burglary of a dwelling while armed, injuring a non-participant, using or threatening a dangerous instrument, or displaying an apparent firearm; it is a class B felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling

intent: With intent to commit a crime therein

penalties.penalty: Class B felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the dwelling or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime is armed with explosives or a deadly weapon

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the dwelling or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime causes physical injury to any person who is not a participant in the crime

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the dwelling or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime uses or threatens the immediate use of a dangerous instrument

crimes.act: Enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
conditions: In effecting entry or while in the dwelling or in immediate flight therefrom, the person or another participant in the crime displays what appears to be a pistol, revolver, rifle, shotgun, machine gun or other firearm
defenses: Affirmative defense: such pistol, revolver, rifle, shotgun, machine gun or other firearm was not a loaded weapon from which a shot, readily capable of producing death or other serious physical injury, could be discharged (this does not bar a prosecution for or conviction of burglary in the second degree, burglary in the third degree or any other crime)

review.plain: Possession of burglar's tools is possessing tools adapted, designed or commonly used for forcible entry, larceny by physical taking, or certain theft of services, intending or knowing they will be so used; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: possesses any tool, instrument or other article adapted, designed or commonly used for committing or facilitating offenses involving forcible entry into premises, or offenses involving larceny by a physical taking, or offenses involving theft of services as defined in subdivisions four, five and six of section 165.15

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Possesses any tool, instrument or other article adapted, designed or commonly used for committing or facilitating offenses involving forcible entry into premises, larceny by a physical taking, or theft of services as defined in subdivisions four, five and six of section 165.15
conditions: Under circumstances evincing an intent to use or knowledge that some person intends to use the same in the commission of an offense of such character

review.plain: Unlawful possession of a radio device is possessing a police-frequency or two-way radio device intending to use it in robbery, burglary, larceny, gambling or an Article 220 violation; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a radio device

intent: With the intent to use that device in the commission of robbery, burglary, larceny, gambling or a violation of any provision of article two hundred twenty of the penal law
terms: "radio device": any device capable of receiving a wireless voice transmission on any frequency allocated for police use, or any device capable of transmitting and receiving a wireless voice transmission

penalties.penalty: Class B misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Possesses a radio device

review.plain: Criminal mischief in the fourth degree covers intentionally damaging another's property, destroying an abandoned building, recklessly damaging property over $250, or disabling emergency communication equipment; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: damages property of another person
participates in the destruction of an abandoned building as defined in section one thousand nine hundred seventy-one-a of the real property actions and proceedings law
damages property of another person in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars
disables or removes telephonic, TTY or similar communication sending equipment

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Damages property of another person
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right

crimes.act: Participates in the destruction of an abandoned building as defined in section one thousand nine hundred seventy-one-a of the real property actions and proceedings law
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right

crimes.act: Damages property of another person
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right
The damage is in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars

crimes.act: Disables or removes telephonic, TTY or similar communication sending equipment
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right

Any of the following: while that person (a) is attempting to seek or is engaged in the process of seeking emergency assistance from police, law enforcement, fire or emergency medical services personnel; or (b) is attempting to seek or is engaged in the process of seeking emergency assistance from another person or entity in order to protect himself, herself or a third person from imminent physical injury
The fact that the defendant has an ownership interest in such equipment shall not be a defense
intent: With intent to prevent a person from communicating a request for emergency assistance

review.plain: Criminal mischief in the third degree is intentionally damaging another's property over $250, or breaking into a locked vehicle to steal after three prior criminal mischief convictions in ten years; it is a class E felony.
acts: damages the motor vehicle of another person, by breaking into such vehicle when it is locked
damages property of another person in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars

penalties.penalty: Class E felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Damages the motor vehicle of another person by breaking into such vehicle when it is locked
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right

Within the previous ten year period, the person has been convicted three or more times, in separate criminal transactions for which sentence was imposed on separate occasions, of criminal mischief in the fourth degree as defined in section 145.00, criminal mischief in the third degree as defined in this section, criminal mischief in the second degree as defined in section 145.10, or criminal mischief in the first degree as defined in section 145.12 of this article
intent: With intent to damage property of another person
With the intent of stealing property

crimes.act: Damages property of another person
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right

intent: With intent to damage property of another person

review.plain: Criminal mischief in the second degree is intentionally damaging another person's property in an amount over $1,500 without right; it is a class D felony.
acts: damages property of another person in an amount exceeding one thousand five hundred dollars

intent: With intent to damage property of another person

penalties.penalty: Class D felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Damages property of another person
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he has such right

review.plain: Criminal mischief in the first degree is intentionally damaging another person's property by means of an explosive without right; it is a class B felony.
acts: damages property of another person by means of an explosive

intent: With intent to damage property of another person

penalties.penalty: Class B felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Damages property of another person by means of an explosive
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he has such right

review.plain: Defines "property of another" for the criminal mischief sections to include any property in which another person has an ownership interest, even if the person damaging it also has one.
Criminal tampering in the third degree is tampering with another person's property without right, intending to cause substantial inconvenience; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: tampers with property of another person

intent: With intent to cause substantial inconvenience to such person or to a third person

crimes.act: Tampers with property of another person
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he has such right

review.plain: Criminal tampering in the second degree is tampering or making connection with utility, carrier or power-plant property without right; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: tampers or makes connection with property of a gas, electric, sewer, steam or water-works corporation, telephone or telegraph corporation, common carrier, nuclear powered electric generating facility, or public utility operated by a municipality or district

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Tampers or makes connection with property of a gas, electric, sewer, steam or water-works corporation, telephone or telegraph corporation, common carrier, nuclear powered electric generating facility, or public utility operated by a municipality or district
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right
defenses: Affirmative defense: the defendant did not engage in such conduct for a larcenous or otherwise unlawful or wrongful purpose

review.plain: Criminal tampering in the first degree is damaging or tampering with utility, carrier or power-plant property to substantially interrupt or impair public service, and causing that interruption; it is a class D felony.
acts: damages or tampers with property of a gas, electric, sewer, steam or water-works corporation, telephone or telegraph corporation, common carrier, nuclear powered electric generating facility, or public utility operated by a municipality or district
causes such substantial interruption or impairment of service

intent: With intent to cause a substantial interruption or impairment of a service rendered to the public

conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right

review.plain: Cemetery desecration in the second degree is intentionally damaging cemetery or grave property, or stealing personal property located at a grave or burial place; it is a class A misdemeanor.

steals personal property which is located at a cemetery plot, grave, burial place or other place of interment of human remains

review.plain: Aggravated cemetery desecration in the second degree is opening an interred casket or crypt and removing remains or objects to obtain unlawful possession of them; it is a class E felony.

unlawfully removes therefrom a body, bodily part, any human remains or any object contained in such casket, crypt or similar vessel

penalties.penalty: Class E felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

crimes.act: Opens a casket, crypt, or similar vessel containing a human body or human remains which has been buried or otherwise interred in a cemetery and unlawfully removes therefrom a body, bodily part, any human remains or any object contained in such casket, crypt or similar vessel
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he or she has such right
intent: For the purpose of obtaining unlawful possession of such body, bodily part, human remains or object for such person or a third person

review.plain: Unlawfully posting advertisements is affixing an advertisement or notice to another's property without right; vendors are presumed to have placed commercial ads; it is a violation.

penalties.penalty: Violation (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he has such right

Where such matter consists of a commercial advertisement, it shall be presumed that the vendor of the specified product, service or entertainment is a person who placed such advertisement or caused it to be placed upon the property

review.plain: Defines "consumer product" for the consumer product tampering sections as any drug, food, beverage or thing offered for sale to the public for ingestion by or application to a human being.
Tampering with a consumer product in the second degree is contaminating a consumer product intending to injure someone or make them fear injury; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: alters, adulterates or otherwise contaminates a consumer product

intent: With intent to cause physical injury to another or with intent to instill in another a fear that he will cause such physical injury

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Alters, adulterates or otherwise contaminates a consumer product
conditions: Having no right to do so nor any reasonable ground to believe that he has such right

review.plain: Tampering with a consumer product in the first degree is contaminating a consumer product to injure or frighten and thereby creating a substantial risk of serious physical injury; it is a class E felony.
acts: alters, adulterates or otherwise contaminates a consumer product and thereby creates a substantial risk of serious physical injury to one or more persons

intent: With intent to cause physical injury to another or with intent to instill in another a fear that he will cause such physical injury

penalties.penalty: Class E felony (sentence set in Penal Law Article 70)

review.plain: Bars throwing or dumping refuse, garbage or offensive matter on railroad tracks or rights-of-way, punishable by a fine of up to $250 and/or up to eight hours of service, more for repeats.
acts: throw, dump, or cause to be thrown, dumped, deposited or placed upon any railroad tracks, or within the limits of the rights-of-way of any railroad, any refuse, trash, garbage, rubbish, litter or any nauseous or offensive matter

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed two hundred fifty dollars and/or a requirement to perform services for a public or not-for-profit corporation, association, institution or agency not to exceed eight hours
A fine not to exceed five hundred dollars and/or a requirement to perform services for a public or not-for-profit corporation, association, institution or agency not to exceed eight hours

crimes.act: Throws, dumps, or causes to be thrown, dumped, deposited or placed upon any railroad tracks, or within the limits of the rights-of-way of any railroad, any refuse, trash, garbage, rubbish, litter or any nauseous or offensive matter
ways: Causes to be thrown, dumped, deposited or placed
exceptions: Where a highway or road lies in whole or part within a railroad rights-of-way, the use in a reasonable manner of ashes, sand, salt or other material for the purpose of reducing the hazard of, or providing traction on snow, ice or sleet situated on such highway or road
A railroad or its employees when matter deposited by them on the railroad tracks or rights-of-way is done pursuant to railroad rules, regulations or procedures

review.plain: Making graffiti is marking any building or other property with intent to damage it without the express permission of the owner or operator; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: make graffiti of any type on any building, public or private, or any other property real or personal owned by any person, firm or corporation or any public agency or instrumentality

penalties.penalty: Class A misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Makes graffiti of any type on any building, public or private, or any other property real or personal owned by any person, firm or corporation or any public agency or instrumentality
conditions: Without the express permission of the owner or operator of said property
terms: "graffiti": the etching, painting, covering, drawing upon or otherwise placing of a mark upon public or private property with intent to damage such property

review.plain: Possession of graffiti instruments is possessing tools or substances made or commonly used to mark property, under circumstances showing intent to use them to damage property one has no permission to mark; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: possesses any tool, instrument, article, substance, solution or other compound designed or commonly used to etch, paint, cover, draw upon or otherwise place a mark upon a piece of property which that person has no permission or authority to etch, paint, cover, draw upon or otherwise mark

penalties.penalty: Class B misdemeanor (sentence set in Penal Law Articles 70 and 80)

crimes.act: Possesses any tool, instrument, article, substance, solution or other compound designed or commonly used to etch, paint, cover, draw upon or otherwise place a mark upon a piece of property which that person has no permission or authority to etch, paint, cover, draw upon or otherwise mark
conditions: Under circumstances evincing an intent to use same in order to damage such property
